speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So how can we make everyone willing to act and willing to contribute?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: What I have experienced as a grassroots advisor in Nee Soon South over the past three years is that, as long as everyone cooperates happily, whether they are employees or volunteers, if they can be accommodating and show gratitute towards each other, they will be able to contribute joyfully and everyone can make a difference.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I believe this is an invaluable way of interaction in our society.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that in the future, through our own practice, we can pass on these values to the next generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A shared future that has been built on the work by all of us and our migrant workers over the past few decades.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As we talk about being an inclusive society, we must not forget our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, our policies at times, show that there is an “us” and “them”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the past eight years as an MP, I have seen firsthand the backbreaking work our migrant workers do for us.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have listened firsthand to the stories of the homes and families they left behind.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I have personally met the families they have left behind and felt the pain they feel every single day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mazibur is a cleaner in Nee Soon East.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He came to Singapore in 2012, leaving his daughter Jannat when she was only 22 days' old.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Jannat will turn 12 years old this year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He has missed all her birthdays and milestones growing up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When I went to Bangladesh a few years ago to meet all our Nee Soon East cleaners' families and have lunch with them, I met Jannat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is sad that I got to meet Mazibur's daughter before he did.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Jannat wrote to me and what she wrote tore through my heart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "Take care of my father, I love him a lot".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many low-wage migrant workers similarly endure long periods of separation from their families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a father of three young girls, I just cannot imagine how painful and how difficult it must be to be so far from their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We enjoy time with our families in the homes that these migrant workers build and keep clean for us.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The least we can do is to take care of them and ensure that these workers have safe living spaces, safe food and safe avenues for reporting illegal employment practices.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a speech delivered at the height of COVID-19, Prime Minister Lee assured our workers, "To our migrant workers, let me emphasise again: we will care for you, just like we care for Singaporeans." I am glad we do care and, over the years, our policies on migrant workers have improved.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this Budget for Singaporeans, I hope we continue to make improvements and remember to care for our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of our youths have set a shining example in caring and speaking up for migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have been inspired by the passion of these youths.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Kari co-founded the migrant worker ground up Sama Sama in 2016.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Sama Sama and their partners support migrant community leaders to address mental health issues, enhance the quality of life and ensure equitable opportunities for migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Migrant worker NGOs like Sama Sama back up their calls with concrete actions through ground-up initiatives to support our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many Singaporeans like Kari are calling for the Government to do more to treat our migrant workers fairly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, we significantly improve the living standards for migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, we ensure the food catered for migrant workers comply with existing food safety standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, we recognise and treat kickbacks as a form of corruption, by ensuring that there are equivalent penalties and whistleblowing protections.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am not asking for any preferential treatment for our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask only that we treat our migrant workers the same way that we would want our loved ones to be treated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask that we be fair and inclusive – have one set of policies that apply to all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first recommendation is that we ensure that the housing standards for dormitories are at least equivalent to the dormitory conditions for our full-time National Servicemen (NSFs).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that MOM announced a set of improved standards for worker dormitories last year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a huge step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By 2030, the dormitories must meet an interim set of housing standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By 2040, the dormitories must meet the new standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOM said that these housing standards are meant to improve the dormitories' ability to contain disease outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that MOM is acting on lessons learnt during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to addressing the public health risks, it is also right that we make sure that our migrant workers have decent living conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, many feel that the interim and new housing standards simply do not go far enough.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our current standards require at least 3.5 square metres per migrant worker.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why the double standards on this question of public health?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are asking for a 0.1-square-metre increase within seven years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another example is the spacing between beds in migrant worker dormitories.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The pandemic taught us hard lessons about how diseases spread like wildfire when people are packed into tiny, cramped dormitory rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, for the next 16 years, we are choosing to accept this risk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are choosing to roll the dice and pray very hard that we will not have another pandemic in the next 16 years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a gamble with the lives of those living in the dormitories and it is a gamble with the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Business costs are rising and employers have financial constraints.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOM has said that dormitory standards cannot improve more quickly because beds are short in supply and rising in price.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Surely, then, the way forward is to study and implement solutions that tackle those problems, rather than wait for them to go away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: JTC used to own and manage dormitories directly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad MOM will be building and owning two migrant-worker purpose-built dormitories (PBDs) through the new entity called NEST Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, it is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOM has announced that the MOM-owned PBDs seek to promote innovations in public health resilience and liveability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They also aim to transform practices in migrant worker housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, if the private market cannot efficiently deliver services at minimum standards and costs necessary for public health, we should ask the hard question of whether Government agencies should reassume the role of managing and operating more dormitories more urgently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By expanding the number of dormitories owned and run by MOM, there would be significant economies of scale and perhaps even lowered costs for employers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It could be a win-win solution for both employers and employees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, we must remember that this is a question of public health.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a life and death issue when, not if, the next pandemic happens.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We already know that the SAF was largely successful in keeping COVID-19 transmissions low.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We already have a successful model to learn from – with a minimum standard of seven square metres per resident and all the measures that SAF took.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All I am asking is that we learn from experience and urgently improve the living conditions of migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second recommendation is that food catered for migrant workers is safe for consumption.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our migrant workers need a proper place to rest and proper food to eat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that MOM recently ensured that there are measures in place that protect catered food from contamination until it is collected by dormitory residents for consumption.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But that solves only one part of the equation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The other parts need to be urgently addressed, too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) requires that all catered food be consumed within four hours after it is prepared.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SFA also requires that all catered food be labelled with a consume-by timestamp.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many Singaporeans will be familiar with these timestamps for catered food or buffets.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This four-hour rule is strictly adhered to for food catered for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, a different set of standard seems to apply for some migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Workers tell me that many of them are catered with food without a consume-by timestamp.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many workers tell me that they regularly consume food way past the four-hour timeframe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is quite obvious that this is true.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We know their catered lunch is cooked in the wee hours of the morning before workers even leave for work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We know the food is delivered to the dormitories early in the morning as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By the time workers have their meal around noon time, the food is way past the four-hour timeframe.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We know for a fact that our requirements are being breached.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) has said that in the past five years, SFA has not received any reported cases of catered food for workers in dormitories without a consume-by timestamp.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOM has also said that they have not received specific complaints from workers about not being able to consume food within a reasonable time of preparation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is at odds with many workers' experiences and the realities on the ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know that MSE and SFA take food safety very seriously.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also know that MOM takes worker safety and welfare very seriously.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My recommendation is that MOM and MSE work together to investigate this and set specific requirements to ensure that catered food is consumed within a safe period.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Migrant workers deserve food that is safe for consumption, just like all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final recommendation is that we recognise and treat kickbacks as a form of corruption.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should ensure that there are equivalent penalties and whistle-blowing protection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That is more than one employer every week being taken to task for collecting kickbacks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, we do not know what the full number of unreported cases is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our laws to protect our workers are only as good as our ability to enforce our laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, their hands were trembling as they spoke to me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They were fearful of the consequences of reporting their bosses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of these workers incur debt to work in Singapore in the first place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Losing their jobs may mean they have no way of repaying the loans they took to work in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One of them told me, "When I came to Singapore in 2016, I paid $14,000.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2018, I paid $1,500 for my Work Permit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Now, they said that if I do not pay them $3,000, they will fire me".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The same worker told me, "I am a really poor man.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this situation, I am really helpless and feeling depressed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am an honest and hardworking man." We can only start solving a problem by calling a spade a spade.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is one spade digging a grave for fairness and inclusiveness.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What kickbacks really are is that they are corrupt gratification that employers coerce from vulnerable workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We also need to make sure we have the same or even stronger whistle-blower protection for informers of corruption for workers to report kickbacks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Prevention of Corruption Act has strong protection for informers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: No complaints can be admitted as evidence in any civil or criminal proceedings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We all know the zero-tolerance approach Singapore takes to corruption.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no reason to treat kickbacks migrant workers pay any differently from other corruption in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the words of Minister Shanmugam, "These workers are here, they are helping us to make Singapore clean.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They form the base of our economy and, therefore, they help us build our prosperity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You know, we say we have 57% of Singaporeans in PMET jobs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is possible because the base is built by foreigners.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I think we have to appreciate what they do for us, and we have to have a better understanding and empathy." I am glad many Singaporeans have shown appreciation for the work migrant workers do for us.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our youths, like Kari, have been calling for our migrant workers to be better protected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said, "We need to do more to look out and care for the more vulnerable amongst us, including our migrant workers".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can start by looking into (a) improving their dormitory standards sooner; (b) ensuring that they have safe catered food; and (c) treating kickbacks as corruption.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The priority in this Budget and in our policies has to be Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it does not mean that our migrant workers should be left out, left behind.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To be the truly inclusive society we aspire to be, a shared future we talk about in this Budget must also include our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To be a fair and just society, we cannot have one set of rules, guidelines and policies for Singaporeans and a different set for migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should look after all our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do this not just because of a promise, but because it is the right thing to do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the start of my speech, I talked about how our policies differentiate between "us" and "them".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have shared this quote in Parliament previously, and I will share it again, "There is no us and them, only us – one human family connected in ways we sometimes forget." I hope our policies can continue to change and recognise that our one human family in Singapore includes our migrant workers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Hazel Poa, you have a clarification to make?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What about a person who starts working at a lower pay grade due to lower qualifications but, subsequently, rose through the ranks to reach the same position as someone with higher qualifications?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does Mr Xie also think that it is fair and right to compensate for the wage gap?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I do not see Mr Xie Yao Quan in the Chamber.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, perhaps, when he is back later and before we conclude the debate, if he wants to clarify, I will allow him.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For now, I will call on Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members have raised many suggestions during this debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will not be able to address all of them in my response.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I assure you that we have heard your feedback and we will study your suggestions carefully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For more detailed issues relating to specific schemes and programmes, these will be addressed later at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The questions raised by Members in this debate largely revolve around three broad issues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Are we doing enough to help Singaporeans cope with higher prices?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How will we achieve better growth and help Singaporeans secure a better future?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Is our system of social support sufficient to support Singaporeans?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let me address these three issues in turn.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, on helping Singaporeans cope with inflation and cost pressures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, including Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Henry Kwek and, Ms Hazel Poa and many others, spoke about this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us start by looking at the reasons for high inflation over the last two years and these reasons are certainly not unique to Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For more than a decade before COVID-19, global inflation was generally stable, hovering at around 4% per annum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore enjoyed relatively stable inflation too, and in most years, it was lower than global inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in 2021, prices in global food, goods, energy markets rose quickly, as strong demand came up against constrained supply due to pandemic-related restrictions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, the Russia-Ukraine war broke out in early 2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The two countries are major suppliers of key commodities, like oil and gas, fertiliser, and wheat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This brought about a further surge in prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many countries also saw a surge in demand for domestic services, and did not have sufficient workers to meet the demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are the key drivers of inflation everywhere and Singapore, like all other countries, felt the impact too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even so, inflation in Singapore did not reach the peaks seen in several parts of the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This meant allowing the Singapore dollar to appreciate more quickly, which helped to shield us against the sharp spike in imported inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, with this overall monetary tightening and the stabilisation of supply chains, significant headway has been made in bringing inflation down around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our inflation too has started coming down, in line with the rest of the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In Singapore, our headline inflation was already moderating since last year, and is expected to moderate further this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We expect this trend to continue, similar to other advanced economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, including Ms Ng Ling Ling, Mr Ong Hua Han and Mr Faisal Manap, also highlighted other specific cost items – namely housing and transport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us drill deeper into this data.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in real terms, the affordability of such BTO flats has, in fact, improved.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The challenge we face was with the prices of BTO flats in choicer locations which are more expensive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have introduced the new Standard, Plus and Prime framework.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because with this framework, we can keep the BTO flats in these better locations affordable through more upfront subsidies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it will be a fair system because the additional subsidies will be clawed back when the first owners sell the flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Or take public transport, the Government is already providing generous subsidies to keep our public transport system going.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fares have increased, but household incomes have risen faster.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why the proportion of household income spent on public transport has fallen over the last 10 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Members are aware, real wage growth was negative last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we know that employers, many of them, are complaining of shortage of workers and higher wage costs, especially in services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is not negative across the board.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some workers were still getting real wage increases.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And at the household level, there was real median income growth, on a per capita basis, per household member basis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In countries everywhere, including in Singapore, there tends to be a gap between economic data and perceptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is partly because it takes time for consumers to adjust to new economic realities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Perceptions and sentiments are clearly important, and we take the feedback from the ground seriously, but we also need to examine data closely so as to better shape policy responses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is in this broader context that the Government had extended support packages over the last two years to cushion the impact of inflation, particularly for lower- and middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have designed and sized the support of the enhancement carefully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is something for everyone, regardless of age, property type, or income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we also do not want to inadvertently stimulate demand too much and push up prices – something which Ms Foo Mee Har cautioned against.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the support is targeted and tilted towards those with less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What will we achieve through the enhancements to the Assurance Package in this Budget?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also helping businesses cope with higher costs, especially SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One of the reasons for rising business costs is higher wages for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we are raising the wages for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it will mean higher costs initially for businesses, especially SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why the Government is doing more in this budget to co-fund the increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Similarly, as Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How highlighted, we are raising CPF contributions for older workers so that they have sufficient savings for retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are doing more to help businesses in this Budget through the Enterprise Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the most generous Corporate Income Tax rebate we have extended to date.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For all eligible firms, including those that are not profitable, we are providing a cash grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The support can be used to defray cost increases, in wages, rentals, utilities, or transport, depending on the circumstances of each business.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand that some groups will feel that the help extended is still not enough.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I hope everyone can appreciate the bigger picture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are going through a rough patch of high prices due to forces well beyond our control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are not the only country facing these difficulties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will do everything we can to help households and businesses to get through this rough patch.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Already, the situation is improving, and it should get better this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But ultimately, the best way to deal with inflation is for businesses and wages to grow in real terms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To achieve that, we need better economic growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This leads me to the second issue – how can we sustain growth and help Singaporeans secure a better future?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And here, many Members spoke up about this, including Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Vikram Nair, amongst others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Securing economic growth is more than just a statistic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about how we stay relevant, add value to the world and make a living for ourselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The reality is that Singapore will always be a little red dot.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have no natural resources, unlike resource-rich countries like Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we falter, no one will come to our rescue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Moreover, businesses have so many options when they wish to invest or site their global or regional headquarters and operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that Singapore is not the cheapest location.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must work even harder to add value and justify the Singapore premium.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is what we have been doing continually since our Independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economy today reflects this progress up the value chain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the example of a multinational enterprise (MNE) like Siemens.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been in Singapore for more than a century, since 1908.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, Siemens today has changed many times over from when it started.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has significantly expanded and upgraded its business, from a small sales office to electronics assembly in the 1970s and now it provides technologies across a range of sectors, including transport systems, water treatment technologies and medical diagnostic equipment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, it announced that it will establish a new high-tech factory in Singapore, which will employ significant levels of automation and digitalisation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Along the way, Siemens has spun off new sub-units, including the semiconductor company Infineon Technologies – which some of you may have heard of – and some of these sub-units have grown into industry leaders in their own right, with their key manufacturing and research and development (R&D) locations based here in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MNEs have continued to grow and upgrade their presence here in Singapore because they value our skilled workforce, our infrastructure and our connectivity to help them better access key markets in the region and beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, when you add it all up, it means that the value-added content of our manufacturing sector has increased.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are able to command better prices in world markets and this in turn benefits our workers, who are able to enjoy higher wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we are able to stay competitive, despite our higher costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One way to see this is to look at Singapore's share of global exports.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since 2010, even when our cost base has gone up, our share of the world’s total goods exports has been maintained at about 2%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our share of global services exports has increased from 2.5% to 4.1%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are able to hold our own, maintain competitiveness and add value, make a living for ourselves, and for our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The question is, how do we continue to maintain or even increase our share of global exports in the years to come?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of this, about one- to 2-percentage points should be from productivity improvements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be clear, this is a very ambitious goal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Only a few countries at our stage of development have been able to sustain such high productivity growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It requires a continual transformation of our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Firms need to learn new ways to do business, workers need to learn new skills to contribute differently and to embrace new technologies, and new firms in new sectors must start up and grow and more than replace the firms in declining industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar and several Members have noted, this is a massive undertaking.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are aiming high and we are determined to do our best to achieve this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some have voiced concerns about whether we will become a two-track economy – one track for MNEs and another for SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I can understand these concerns, but it is not so helpful to think of the economy in terms of larger foreign and smaller local companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A better way is to consider the two broad segments of the economy: one that is outward-oriented and another that is domestic-oriented.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every economy, including Singapore, has these two segments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The outward-oriented segment of the economy comprises MNEs, but it also has many local enterprises, big and small.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And there are many supplier and partnership arrangements between MNEs and local firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to encourage more of these partnerships and we have enhanced the PACT scheme in this Budget to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Companies in this outward-oriented segment are generally more productive and also have some scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have to be; they compete in the global marketplace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They must continuously innovate and up their game.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Otherwise, they will fall behind and they will lose their share of the global market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Not surprisingly, these companies have high take-up of Government schemes that help them invest in R&D, automation and productivity improvements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They do not need to be persuaded to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The remaining 25% of our economy comprises mainly domestic-oriented sectors like F&B, retail and construction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are, of course, also domestic services which are high touch in nature, like childcare and elderly care, and they require workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, these domestic oriented sectors tend to be less productive than the outward-oriented sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is the same for all other economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the productivity of some of our domestic-oriented sectors lags behind similar sectors in other advanced economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The productivity of our construction sector is about one quarter that of Switzerland.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, within our domestic-oriented sectors, there is a range of firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some are embracing change and restructuring themselves to be more productive, others are less ready to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we can and we must do more to encourage and support companies, especially SMEs, in this restructuring journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members spoke about this, including Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr Keith Chua, Mr Neil Parekh, Mr Derrick Goh, and Mr Mark Lee, and we will consider all of your suggestions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we also have to be careful that Government support does not inadvertently prop up outdated or unviable business models and hinder restructuring.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why our support schemes are geared towards supporting business owners who are themselves prepared to embrace change and to adopt new and more productive solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is what we have done and will continue to do.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While we push hard on productivity growth, we also need our workforce to grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is one issue that comes up repeatedly in all our engagements with businesses, especially SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They just cannot find enough workers, and they tell us all the time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of the increase in the workforce will come from growing our resident workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we know that the increase in our own resident workforce has been slowing and will not be sufficient to meet the demands of our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it will have to be complemented by a continued inflow of foreign work pass holders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We already have in place a comprehensive system of controls to regulate the quality and the number of incoming work pass holders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This applies across every level of the workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the lower end of the income spectrum, we have Work Permit holders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They comprise about two-thirds of our total foreign workforce and mostly take up roles that Singaporeans do not want to do, for example, in construction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have not loosened our Work Permit controls.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But even at present settings, firms are able to bring in more workers, because of the demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are building more public housing, more residential housing projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are ramping up or going ahead with major infrastructure projects like the MRT, Changi T5, Tuas Port.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Workers are needed to build these projects, and so the firms are bringing in more of them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will ensure, as Mr Louis Ng said just now very eloquently, we must make sure that we take care of these workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will ensure we have the necessary infrastructure to accommodate these workers well, including building more dormitories – dormitories with the revised standards that we have put in place based on our COVID-19 experience and more recreational centres for their well-being.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is something we owe to these workers who help to build our country.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the middle-income levels, we have Singaporeans doing the jobs, but there are not enough of us, and that is why we top up with S Pass holders and they include people doing important jobs like nurses and technicians.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So far, S Pass numbers have been stable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to make sure that S Pass holders have the right skillsets and are in areas where we need them the most.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the higher end of the income spectrum, we have Employment Pass (EP) holders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are professionals with the skills and abilities to contribute at the upper end of the workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is especially so for new growth areas like AI and the digital economy, where there is currently a shortage of skilled talent, not just in Singapore but also globally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We apply salary cut-offs to ensure that the EP holders we bring in are of the right calibre.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, we have stated previously that we aim for EP holders to be comparable in quality to the top one-third of our local PMET workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Manpower will share more details of the changes at its Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not a new policy setting because the policy intent to ensure that the salary cutoffs are comparable in quality to the top one-third of our local PMET workforce has already been stated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not to chase after a target.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not to grow for the sake of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is to secure better outcomes for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why, in tandem, we are making several other major moves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This reflects the Government’s commitment to push against discrimination in the workforce and ensure fair employment opportunities for all workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are investing more heavily in Singaporeans, something which many Members spoke passionately about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we give our people the extra advantage to compete and excel in the global marketplace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, in this Budget, we are making significant enhancements to SkillsFuture and introducing new schemes to help our workers realise their full potential, regardless of their start points or stage of career.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we have focused on the segments that face more challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For young ITE graduates, we introduced the ITE Progression Award to encourage and support their upskilling journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan and Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With this award, they will be better supported and they will have many opportunities to get an MOE-funded diploma, not just in the polytechnics, but also at other institutions like ITE, where they offer work-study programmes, as well as technical diplomas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want our ITE students to do well, deepen their skills and go further.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Get on a better career and wage trajectory in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This Progression Award will encourage and support them in this journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members, including Leader of the Opposition Mr Pritam Singh, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Gerald Giam, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Syed Harun, all spoke about this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There were many suggestions, such as to expand the scope of the SkillsFuture Credit, to reduce the qualifying age or to provide additional incentives and support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Level-Up programme is a significant new addition to our SkillsFuture system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have not even talked about the details yet, which will be announced by the Minister for Education at COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will make this first move, we will consider all your feedback and suggestions, and how to further finetune and enhance the scheme, as we gain more experience over time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is another segment we are paying close attention to, that is, Singaporeans with the potential to take on leadership positions in MNEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over time, more Singaporeans have taken on such regional and global leadership roles, and we want to nurture and grow this pipeline of Singaporean leaders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Naturally, there is intense competition for these highly sought-after jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The MNEs will and should rightfully select and appoint their leaders by merit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But when companies look for or consider people for such roles, they will typically look for those who have already spent substantial time managing an overseas operation, because remember, they are looking for regional and global leaders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, you must have spent time overseas, running, managing overseas operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means that Singaporeans who would like to be considered for these positions must be prepared to be posted overseas, not just in your early 20s, when many young people like to be posted overseas, but also in your 30s and 40s when you are taking on managerial responsibilities and also when you have settled down and have families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Understandably, at that season in life, relocating overseas is not going to be easy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The spouse may have to stop work for some time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over time, I am confident we can develop and nurture more Singaporean experts and leaders across all fields.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are our plans to secure better growth and better opportunities for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is also how we take concrete steps towards helping everyone realise their Singapore Dream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This idea of a refreshed Singapore Dream was expressed by the vast majority of Singaporeans, especially our youths, during our Forward Singapore engagements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be clear, it does not mean that Singaporeans have given up on material goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they want to avoid getting trapped in an endless rat race of hyper-competition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They want to find meaning and fulfilment in what they do, beyond material success.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are undoubtedly some generational shifts because these aspirations are perhaps more commonly expressed amongst those born after Independence than before.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: My colleagues and I in the 4G leadership, almost all of us were born after Independence too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, perhaps, we instinctively empathise with these aspirations, and as part of Forward Singapore and as a first step in this Budget, we are doing more to help our fellow Singaporeans realise these shared aspirations – by providing more opportunities and diverse pathways for everyone to excel, to develop to their fullest potential and to be the best possible version of themselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore must be defined not just by how far our talents can go, but also by how well we support one other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this new environment, we recognise that there will be more stresses and strains on our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With rapid technological advances and more intense competition, we can expect more churn at workplaces.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some jobs will become obsolete while new jobs with better pay will be created.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All this will be very unsettling for those who are affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This brings me to the third issue we have to address: is our system of social support sufficient to assure Singaporeans through every life stage?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Again, many Members spoke passionately about this – Mr Dennis Tan, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Dr Wan Rizal, just to name a few.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we have been working hard over the years to progressively enhance our social safety nets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started in a more deliberate manner around the Asian Financial Crisis in 1997 when we first saw income trends diverging.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have continued to fine-tune and improve over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we are taking further steps to strengthen our system of risk pooling and social support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The traditional pillars in any social support system are education, housing, healthcare, work and retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In education, we have invested heavily in a first-class school system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also significantly increased our investments in preschool education, and expanded tertiary education options for our youths, including increases to the university cohort participation rates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In housing, we have public housing and the Housing and Development Board (HDB).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We celebrate 60 years of the Home Ownership Scheme this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a significant milestone because there is no other institution like the HDB in the world, which has provided comprehensively for the housing needs of its people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, it may even be misleading to call it “public housing”, because when you look around the world, public housing elsewhere often develops into slums or even ghettos.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our public housing is really a national housing scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And our housing policies are not static – we continue to review and update them and remain fully committed to keeping our national housing affordable and accessible for Singaporeans, including those from lower-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In healthcare, we have Government subsidies and the 3Ms – MediSave, MediShield, and MediFund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We made MediShield universal and lifelong through MediShield Life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Recently, we have launched Healthier SG and Age Well SG.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In work, we have strived to create good jobs for all Singaporeans, not only to provide a good living, but also because work gives dignity and purpose in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To uplift our lower-wage workers, we have added Workfare and Progressive Wages, as noted by Mr Raj Joshua Thomas and many others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In retirement, we have the Central Provident Fund (CPF), which we have been enhancing over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We pay additional interest to help those with lower balances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We introduced CPF LIFE because Singaporeans are living longer, and we want to provide them with a retirement payout for life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We provide Silver Support for seniors who had low incomes during their working years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And now, we have the Majulah Package to help seniors accumulate more retirement savings, especially our young seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are continuously studying how we can do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those who ask for higher CPF returns, you will surely know that higher returns must come with higher risks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To what extent can retirees bear this volatility, especially when they may need to withdraw their funds in a period of negative investment returns in the markets?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are some of the complex issues that the Government has to weigh and consider carefully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in the end, we will ensure that the CPF system provides for the basic retirement needs of all Singaporeans so long as they work and contribute to their CPF consistently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Around these five pillars, which I have just described, we have ComCare – to ensure that no family and no individual falls through the cracks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through ComCare we provide financial assistance, short- and medium-term as well as long-term assistance to those in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we have gone beyond just providing financial support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We lean forward to take a more family-centric approach – bringing together different agencies and community partners, and customising support for lower-income families, especially those with young children, through ComLink, and now, ComLink+.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also provided more support for vulnerable groups, such as children with special needs, ex-offenders and persons with disabilities, something which several Members spoke passionately about, including Mr Eric Chua, Miss Rachel Ong, Mr Ong Hua Han.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The latest addition to our system is SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have made good progress, but we still need to do more, and that is why we have made significant enhancements to SkillsFuture in this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also working on the new support scheme for those who are involuntarily unemployed as part of our enhancements to SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, this is really more of a jobseeker support scheme than an unemployment benefit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We considered whether or not to make this an insurance scheme, but for an insurance scheme to work, it will require universal enrolment, otherwise, the insurers will be cherry picking.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There will be what economists call "adverse selection".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we make it mandatory, or require universal enrolment, this will require contributions from employers and employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, all of us as taxpayers and the Government will help you bounce back if you face unemployment setbacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are working out the parameters and will share more details later this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have been strengthening them year after year, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why over the last 20 years, social spending by the Government has quadrupled.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a share of the Budget, we are also spending more on social support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A substantial portion of this is spent on structural schemes, not temporary measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some Members would like the Government to do even more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But other members have reminded us that the Government should proceed carefully, so as not to breed a sense of entitlement, dependency or undermine individual responsibility and self-reliance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, we are very careful about getting this balance right.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have not changed our ethos of social support – it is not about giving handouts, but giving people a leg-up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: ComLink+ and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme have been designed so as not to erode personal and family responsibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, the upcoming scheme providing temporary support for those who are involuntarily unemployed will also abide by these principles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We catch Singaporeans when they fall and make sure they do not fall behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We invest in them and provide them the support to bounce back from life’s setbacks and do even better for themselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the end, this is about ensuring that families and individuals enjoy better incomes and better living standards.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you look over the past decade, the lower-income groups in Singapore have, in fact, progressed faster than the rest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is based on incomes alone, it has not taken in consideration our progressive system of taxes and benefits which favours the lower-income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, if you were to add all of that together, the overall picture is in fact, better for the lower-income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to work hard to keep on improving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We learn from other countries, and we are open to all ideas – from Members of Parliament, researchers, and community advocates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will consult widely and make bold and effective changes to take Singapore and Singaporeans forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During this debate, many Members – Opposition MPs, PAP MPs, Labour MPs – all of you have laid claim to the policy shifts announced in the Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Well, I am glad everyone wants to be associated with the Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As the saying goes, failure is an orphan, but success has many fathers, and mothers too, I should add!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Basically, we welcome all who wish to associate themselves with these forward-thinking initiatives, because in truth, no one has a monopoly on ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many stakeholders also outside this House who have claimed credit and in fact, who have shared with us many ideas too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has and will continue to provide more information to facilitate informed discussions of policies, something which several Members spoke about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) publishes the Singapore Public Sector Outcomes Report every two years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This covers a broad range of outcome indicators.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We continue to finetune and improve this report.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us have you feedback and suggestions on what additional indicators we should track and we should incorporate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking ahead, there will be even more opportunities for ground-up and civic engagements, something which Ms He Ting Ru, Dr Tan Wu Meng and Ms Denise Phua spoke about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will provide more platforms for individuals and groups to contribute meaningfully, not just through feedback sessions, but also youth panels, citizens’ panels where participants play active roles to co-create and update policies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And in the end, the real work is about translating ideas into effective policies that work for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We all want better wages, better assurance, better security for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But what is the effective way to achieve these goals?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many things start from good intentions, but they do not all achieve what is intended.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are the careful deliberations that have to be made.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we look at the many policies the Government has introduced over the years, it is clear that we are different from what other countries do.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is because we do not just blindly copy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are not ashamed to say that we do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We adapt to our own needs, we discuss with key stakeholders, especially our tripartite partners to get buy-in and then, we develop something that applies to our context.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not just about changing the words.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This reflects our policy emphases and priorities and how we go about effecting change for the betterment of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that we may not always get it right, but we will always improve and keep on doing better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to evolve and improve our system of social support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will maintain the right incentives, actively enable self-reliance and make sure we are able to fund these schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we sustain a social trampoline that promotes rather than dulls economic progress that ensures the fruit of progress is shared by all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how a strong economy and a strong society coexist and reinforce each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take education for example – we provide quality education that produces results.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have one of the highest mean scores in reading, mathematics and science in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our long-term and prudent approach has enabled us to keep Government expenditure at less than one-fifth of GDP – 20% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has in turn allowed us to keep our tax burden low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, 40% of all workers do not pay personal income tax.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The effective tax burden for middle-income households – at around 10% of household income – is significantly lower than other advanced economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: UK and Finland, for example, have middle-income tax burdens that exceed 30%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our fiscal system is also fair and progressive: where those with greater needs receive more help than what they pay in taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But how does this compare with other countries?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are some inherent limitations in comparing across countries but we have done some computations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore, in fact, does better than advanced economies, like the UK and Finland, especially for lower and middle-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the statistics that I mentioned just now also do not include other intangible benefits – like access to quality education, healthcare, housing or having safe streets in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we provide and take care of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, a progressive system must mean that the better-off contribute more and this includes paying more in Property Tax for those with higher-value homes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the Annual Value (AV) band changes that we have announced in the Budget, the higher owner-occupied Property Tax rates will apply to those living in homes with AVs above S$40,000 – or the top 7% of properties in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, within this group, there is also a range and those who pay a lot more in Property Taxes generally have homes with much higher value – we are talking about higher-end condominiums, semi-detached houses, bungalows and Good Class Bungalows.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
